transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-11-11
Start: 10:30 PST
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Aileen Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Rina Patel (Catalyst, Head of ML), Jonas Weber (Catalyst, Platform Eng), Marta Ruiz (Catalyst, CTO)

Summary:
Quick weekly pilot sync focused on unit economics (tokens/sec/$), caching experiment results, batching tradeoffs and next steps for a production pilot on private deployment. Agreed next experiments and delivery dates, ask for SOC 2 docs and a throughput window for a dedicated benchmark.

Topics:
- Recent pilot numbers: tokens/sec/$ trends
- KV/prefix cache effects on token costs
- Batching: throughput vs p95 latency
- Networking and VPC concerns for pilot
- Compliance docs (SOC2, KMS)

Action items (recap below as structured items)

Transcript:
00:00 Aileen: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh it's 10:30 here, hope that's all good, we'll run about 50 minutes and focus on the econ stuff first
00:12 Rina: yeah sounds good, we've got a couple engineers in the room, jonas and i will jump in on the bench marks
00:18 Jonas: morning, thanks. quick note we ran the last staging run overnight, saw some curious token delta across prompts
00:26 Marcus: ok, cool, i'll pull that up—so the headline, uh from Redwood side, we've been tracking tokens per second per dollar, we saw roughly a 23% improvement after the kv prefix cache landed
00:40 Rina: 23% wow, that's promising, what was the baseline again? was that the 2.7b model or the 13b? i think we started on 6b
00:50 Marcus: it's the 13b variant quantized, baseline was about 1.8k tokens/sec/$ on the hosted bucket, after cache it's at 2.2k — numbers are a bit noisy because of variance in seq lengths
01:05 Marta: when you say cache, you mean the prefix KV cache, like the prefix-level reuse? just want to make sure we're talking same thing
01:12 Marcus: yep, prefix KV cache; effectively we store the common prompt keys so subsequent calls that share the same opening 256 tokens hit the cache and skip compute for those tokens
01:23 Rina: what hit rate did you see? real world workloads for us are maybe 30–40% reused prompts not 80
01:31 Marcus: good point—on our synthetic runs we hit 62% with warm-up traffic, but with your mixed corpus the estimate dropped to ~38% which maps to about 9–11% cost savings on tokens
01:44 Jonas: ok, so it's not as dramatic as synthetic but still solid. can we trade batching for more savings? we noticed p95 spiked in some of the runs
01:53 Marcus: yep batching is the other lever. We ran batch sizes 8 and 32; throughput jumps significantly at 32 but p95 goes up from 180ms to about 420ms on p95 for the 13b on the dedis config
02:09 Aileen: just to clarify, when you say dedis config that's our dedicated pool with 8xA10G — there's also a hosted variant which has slightly different kernel selection
02:19 Jonas: yeah and for our latency-sensitive product, p95 over 300ms is a problem during checkout flows
02:27 Marta: so what's the sweet spot? batch 8? or smaller? we care about tokens/sec/$ but not at the expense of checkout latency
02:35 Marcus: in our runs batch 8 gives you ~60% of the max throughput while keeping p95 sub-220ms. batch 16 is a compromise but p95 creeps toward 280–320ms depending on sequence length
02:49 Rina: could we do adaptive batching? like dynamic batch size under load so hotspots use smaller batches
02:57 Marcus: yes, Redwood runtime supports dynamic batching policies, you can set a latency SLO and it will throttle batch sizes. there is sometimes a small throughput tax for the controller overhead but it's usually acceptable
03:13 Jonas: do you have numbers on the controller overhead? like tokens/sec/$ delta from adaptive control
03:19 Marcus: rough ballpark, about 3–6% throughput loss compared to fixed max batching, but p95 improves significantly for tail requests
03:28 Rina: good to know. on the cache experiment, can we try a lower memory kv window — we saw memory constraints on the 8x pool
03:36 Marcus: absolutely, one knob is kv window size and also which layers to cache. We can trim to first 128 tokens and see hit rate vs memory impact, that should cut mem usage ~30%
03:47 Marta: are there any quality regressions from caching? does it affect streaming or function calling behavior?
03:53 Marcus: caching is just skipping compute for cached keys, it doesn't change model outputs — but there are corner cases with session state if you mutate system prompts mid-session, so best practice is to pin the prompt structure for cached flows
04:07 Rina: noted. ok, we also wanted to ask about encryption/KMS — for the private pilot we need customer-managed keys and HSM, can you confirm support?
04:16 Aileen: yes, Redwood Private supports customer KMS and integrates with common HSM providers. we have a quickstart doc, i'll send it after the call
04:23 Jonas: also SSO for engineers, SAML + RBAC needed before we open the prod environment to non-alpha team
04:30 Aileen: that's part of the private package, SAML + SCIM and RBAC roles are supported. we can share our role mapping examples
04:36 Rina: perfect. on the economics spreadsheet you sent, there's a row for "tokens/sec/$ (incl cache)"—can you explain the formula used
04:45 Marcus: sure, it's tokens served per second divided by effective $/sec for the cluster. effective $/sec takes into account reserved capacity amortization plus per-request costs for hosted. For private we amortize the VM/gpu cost across provisioned hours
04:59 Marta: so for our case with 40% expected reuse, what's the projected tokens/sec/$ if we run dedicated and use prefix cache plus batch 8?
05:08 Marcus: quick estimate—if baseline is 1.8k t/s/$ hosted, dedicated with cache + batch8 at 40% reuse would be around 2.6–2.8k tokens/sec/$,pero—excuse me—per the pilot numbers
05:20 Rina: that would be great. can you share a sensitivity table—reuse 20/40/60 vs batch sizes
05:26 Marcus: yeah i'll produce that as part of the runbook, sensitivity table with the major knobs
05:32 Jonas: one more question on routing—if capacity is constrained, does Redwood automatically fall back to smaller model or to hosted tier?
05:40 Aileen: yes you can configure smart routing policies. you can set preference order: dedicated first, fallback to smaller quantized variant, then hosted if needed. policies can be per-route
05:52 Marta: ok how disruptive is a fallback in terms of outputs? are there measurable quality deltas we should expect
05:58 Marcus: smaller model will generally have increased hallucination risk and slightly shorter context handling, we'll flag any quality delta in evals and you can add automatic regressions alerts
06:07 Rina: timeline check—we need pilot results by end of month for exec review. can we hit that with these experiments?
06:13 Aileen: yes, with the runs we've planned we should have a combined cost/latency report by 11/27
06:19 Jonas: can we book a 2-hour slot for the dedicated throughput benchmark on 11/20? need to cut load across 3 configs
06:25 Aileen: i'll propose times after this call
06:29 Marcus: quick note on observability—we'll enable token-level cost breakdown and per-route p95 traces, you'll get a dashboard with per-prompt token counts
06:37 Rina: great. last question, do you have any recommendations to reduce inference cost aside from cache and batch?
06:43 Marcus: yes, quantization profiles are powerful—switching to 4-bit quant can drop runtime cost 25–40% depending on model and accuracy tolerance. also early exit / output truncation strategies for few-shot prompts
06:56 Marta: do you have empirical perf numbers for the 4-bit quant for our 13b?
07:01 Marcus: early numbers show about 30% improvement tokens/sec/$ with minimal quality loss in our evals but we'll run your prompt suite to validate
07:10 Rina: ok perfect. let's recap next steps quickly
07:14 Aileen: recap — Marcus to run kv window and batch sensitivity and produce spreadsheet; Marcus to include reuse sensitivity and quant results; Jonas to schedule dedicated throughput run 11/20; Aileen to send SOC2/KMS docs and propose times; all by dates noted
07:29 Jonas: noted
07:30 Rina: sounds good, thanks
07:32 Marta: thanks everyone

End of transcript
